commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved. (claude.ai sync)

content.text: I'll start by loading the Lumail skill and checking which local tools are available.

content.content: Launching skill: lumail

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/melvynx/.claude/skills/lumail

Use the global `lumail` command for every call. It must resolve to `/opt/homebrew/bin/lumail`, which runs the current CLI from the active production repository.

```bash
command -v lumail
lumail --version
lumail admin --help
```

Verify these before the first API call. Require the Homebrew path, the expected current version, and the `admin` command; a version string alone is insufficient because an incomplete npm artifact may report the same version. Pass `--json` for parsing and never print raw tokens.

Inspect `lumail --help`, then `<resource> --help` and `<resource> <action> --help`. Never invent flags.

The default credential on this machine is the platform admin token. When a URL contains `/orgs/<orgSlug>/`, extract the slug and pass `--organization <orgSlug>` on every org-scoped command. Before the first mutation, run `admin orgs get <orgSlug> --json` and verify the returned slug. Do not use `--account <orgSlug>` for the admin token.

For platform-wide work with a `luma_` admin API key:

```bash
lumail admin orgs list --search <query> --json
lumail admin orgs get <id-or-slug> --json
lumail <resource> <action> --organization <id-or-slug>
```

`--organization` is required on every org-scoped command when the token is `luma_`. Same home-page filters as Admin → Organizations: `--search`, `--plan`, `--status`, `--activity`, `--click-domain`, `--double-opt-in`, `--limits`.

For anything beyond ordinary reads, inspect the live catalog first:

    lumail tools list --raw --organization <orgSlug>
    lumail tools get <tool-name> --organization <orgSlug>
    lumail tools run <tool-name> --params '<json>' --organization <orgSlug> --json

If catalog listing fails, inspect the required tool directly with `tools get`. Preserve schema enum case.

`campaigns update` is metadata only. Edit bodies with `tools run edit_campaign`. MAILY: `content` (TipTap JSON) or `operations`, never both. HTML: full-string `content` plus `contentType: "HTML"` — operations are rejected. Call `get_skill` with `{"type":"campaign"}` before writing a body. Load `get_skill` with `{"type":"images"}` or `{"type":"workflow"}` before image-fit or workflow-graph work. `configure_workflow_draft` is atomic; refresh `expectedUpdatedAt` and retry the same complete payload on timeout.

Prefer `tools run` for send, schedule, unsubscribe, reactivation, bulk tags, or delete. Dangerous tools return a confirmation code; repeat the exact args plus `confirmationCode`. Do not retry a stale code.

For local Markdown drafts, read `/Users/melvynx/cc/.agents/skills/lumail-local-draft/SKILL.md`. For evergreen funnel audits, read `/Users/melvynx/cc/.agents/skills/review-evergreen-codeline-lumail/SKILL.md`. Load these guides only for the matching task.

After campaign edits, read back the saved campaign and render it to verify the content and footer. Preserve the user's voice and draft status unless another action is requested.

Reply in the user's language with a concise summary of the result, a campaign link, and any unresolved items. Return raw JSON only when the user explicitly requests it.

## Overview
Lumail is a modern email marketing tool built for AI agents, allowing you to easily migrate, manage campaigns, and pay only for emails sent. Melvyn Xueref created Lumail.io, which he uses to send his marketing emails, and built it in one week as a clone of Mailchimp or other tools with automation, tagging, etc.

## Key Features
Lumail brings email campaigns, automated sequences and transactional messages into one platform, with an AI-assisted editor and MCP, API, CLI and SDK access to help you prepare and manage sends.

Specific capabilities include:
- AI-assisted editor with variables, conditional blocks and preview before sending
- Automation with sequences featuring delays, branches and goals, then A/B testing of steps
- Agent integration via MCP to prepare campaigns and segment lists, with a REST API, CLI and TypeScript SDK
- Import subscribers via CSV, organize lists, tags and segments, and track opens, clicks and conversions
- Transactional email sending through a priority queue separate from campaigns

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". The 45-second Lumail launch video is done, saved as `video.mp4` with a minimal `index.html` player next to it. I opened the player in headless Chrome at three viewport sizes and the video played at each.

**Checks**
- **MP4:** 1920×1080 H.264, 30 fps, exactly 45.000 s, about 4.8 MB.
- **Player:** In headless Chrome at 1920×1080, 1000×900 and 1400×500, the video played with no errors and its box stayed at exactly 16:9. It fills the full width or height, letterboxed with black, with no cropping or distortion.
- **Encoded frames:** I pulled frames from the MP4 itself at 4.2 s (a transition), 29 s and 44.9 s. The 29 s frame is the migration scene mid-animation, so the stat counters still read 0 there.
- **Player page:** The browser title is "Claude Sonnet 5.5" and there is no visible heading. Native playback controls are on.

**Video**
- **Research:** I used public sources only: lumail.io, its stylesheet, and web search. The design matches the site: warm off-white background, black Geist type, an orange-red `#ff3300` accent with a 3D button, white pill highlights, and the red "L" logo.
- **Story:** The video runs through these scenes:
  1. Hook: "Email marketing shouldn't feel like a second job."
  2. Brand reveal: "The AI Tool that will make you love e-mail marketing."
  3. An AI agent tagging 312 subscribers.
  4. The email editor.
  5. A workflow sequence.

  8. Pricing: "You pay for emails sent. Never for subscribers."

  10. An end card with "Start free · 3,000 emails/month · no card · lumail.io."
- **Transitions:** Orange and black wipes join the scenes.

The video has no audio track. The frames were rendered from HTML with Chrome and encoded with ffmpeg. The build files are in `work/`, but `video.mp4` and `index.html` don't need them.
